provenance.notes: Numerical observations copied from the private capture records K-C (task 9396), K-C2 (task 9460) and K-C5 (task 9483); the private findings remain the source of record. Base-drag rows (task 9473): K-C (C1a, C1a3, C1d, C1e, C1e sphere), K-C2 (C2d_top_box(_ctrl), C2e_sph / _cyl / C2e1_cone / C2e2_caps, C2f_torus, C2c_psp_box) and K-C3 (C3a / C3b corners, tests/unit).

_about: A create click over a BACKGROUND surface with the surface constraint on (geometry off, double-sided off, snapping off unless stated). Background: a sphere of radius 1, 64 sides x 32 segments, centre (0,1,0), in a background layer; the foreground mesh starts empty. ROLE law: a FREE point (the vertex tool's click) reads the surface, a primitive's PRESS point (box corner, sphere centre) does not. The free point: q = the click's anchor-plane hit snapped to the view quantum (the create click law); the background hit on the VIEW ray through q (parallel in ortho, from the eye in perspective) wins, NOT re-quantised; offset * hit normal after it; no hit => q; then a snap target replaces all three channels. The surface height is a depth read at the reference (1/1024 lattice in ortho, ~1e-3 off a facet model; up to ~8e-3 along the ray in perspective; the offset normal 1-2 deg off the facet): compare the ray / in-plane channels to 1e-5 and heights to the cell's own scatter, floor 2e-3. BASE DRAG (box second corner; sphere / cylinder / cone / capsule / torus radius point): the press corner Pq = q(press plane hit) is carried by the pointer's pixel travel through the plane map linearised at Pq (a forward difference of ten view pixels; exact as Pq + (R - P) in top and straight-down views) to T; the constraint taking the pointer and the eye ray through T meeting the background => that hit + offset * n, NOT quantised; otherwise q(T); the base-plane channel stays Pq's; then the snap.

box-press-plane.law: PLANE: the press corner is the quantised plane point; the surface (y 1.930664) is not read at the press

box-press-plane-persp.law: PLANE-RAY: press corner = q(plane hit); the projected surface hit lies 0.095 m away

sphere-press-plane.law: PLANE: the centre is the quantised plane point

vertex-surface-top.law: SURF: xz = q, height = the surface on the vertical ray through q

vertex-surface-offset.source: K-C C1e on the vertex tool
vertex-surface-offset.law: OFF-AFTER-Q: the surface point on the q-ray + 0.1 * hit normal (the reference normal is a depth-read normal 1-2 deg off the facet, so every channel carries up to offset * sin(2 deg) = 3.5e-3)

vertex-surface-handle-off.source: K-C5 (task 9483) on the vertex tool: handle 0 => PLANE (0.3, 1.0, 0.2) exactly, geometry off and Point alike; no surface query runs
vertex-surface-handle-off.law: handle off: the constraint does not take the pointer; the click is the plane point

vertex-surface-persp.law: SURF on the eye ray through q, off the q lattice (captured (0.260365, 1.948835, 0.166987) on the reference camera)

outside-vertex-surface-persp-coarse-a.outside: at the recorded camera our pixel lattice (~0.054 m at the plane) has no pixel whose raw hit lies inside the recorded q cell (0.6, -0.8): nearest 0.0268 > q/2 on one channel, so our click cannot reach the recorded q; the two other coarse reads stand

vertex-surface-persp-coarse-b.source: K-C2 C2c3H_pspax_vtx (the reference vertex was dragged to this pixel; ours places at the press, so the cell clicks the release pixel)

vertex-surface-turned-top.law: QPLANE-RAY under a pinned plane: frame-local xz = q, the frame height = the surface on the frame-vertical ray

vertex-surface-snap.source: K-C2 C2i_vtx (snapping off, C2i_vtx_ctrl lands on the surface at (0.13, 1.96875, 0.2))
vertex-surface-snap.law: SNAP-LAST: a foreground vertex in range replaces all three channels of the surface point; the vertex tool does not weld (nv 2)

box-drag-surface.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); surface on: the vertical ray through T, unquantised

box-drag-handle-off.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); handle off: q(T); the old K-C law (q of the release plane point) gives the same (0.4, 0.3) here

box-drag-miss.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); the ray through T misses the background: q(T); the old law gives the same (1.26, 0.3) here

box-drag-surface-offset.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); surface hit + 0.1 * hit normal, in-plane channels (the reference normal is a depth-read normal, 1-2 deg off the facet: tolerance 2e-3)

box-drag-surface-top.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); surface on: T unquantised (0.654545 vs the control's 0.65)

box-drag-off-control.law: T = Pq + (pixel travel) / px_per_m (top view: the map is exact); constraint off: q(T) = Pq + q(R - P), not q(R) = (0.7, -0.6)

box-drag-persp-down.source: K-C2 C2c_psp_box (straight-down perspective; the camera is ours, so the cell asserts the law on OUR camera)
box-drag-persp-down.law: straight down the map is affine: Pq = q(our press ray's plane hit); T = Pq + (R - P) from our own press / release rays; the corner is the background hit on the eye ray through T, its xz written, y the base plane's: cross-trace <= 1e-5, the hit on the background within the facet sagitta

sphere-drag-surface.law: one drag point for the radial family: the radii are |D - Pq| per in-plane channel, D = the box's drag point

cylinder-drag-surface.law: one drag point for the radial family: the radii are |D - Pq| per in-plane channel, D = the box's drag point

cone-drag-surface.law: one drag point for the radial family: the radii are |D - Pq| per in-plane channel, D = the box's drag point

capsule-drag-surface.law: one drag point for the radial family: the radii are |D - Pq| per in-plane channel, D = the box's drag point

torus-drag-surface.source: K-C2 C2f_torus (the same bbox as the sphere: the same drag point)
torus-drag-surface.law: the torus' drag point is the radial family's D; ours' ring radius is |D - Pq| (one radius, gap row 566: the reference's in-plane extents are per channel), 1.066724 = |(0.752165, 0.756387)|

sphere-drag-surface-offset.law: centre on the plane (Pq); the offset reaches only the drag point: radii |D - Pq|
